# Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam International Foundation — fact sheet

Last updated: 2026-10-28
Website: https://www.apjabdulkalamfoundation.org/

## Summary

The Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam International Foundation is a registered public charitable trust based at the House of Kalam in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu. It carries forward the vision of Bharat Ratna Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, India's eleventh President, through STEM and space education, environmental work, skilling and peace programmes for young people, with a focus on government schools and underserved communities.

## At a glance

- Legal status: Registered public charitable trust (12A and 80G; Form CSR-1 registered)
- Founded: 11 October 2015
- Founded by: The family and close colleagues of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
- Seat: House of Kalam, Rameswaram – 623 526, Ramanathapuram District, Tamil Nadu, India
- Focus: STEM and space education, environment, skilling, peace
- Reach: Students across India; programmes abroad (Bahrain, United Nations)
- Guiding idea: Dr. Kalam's Vision 2020 for a developed India

## Impact

- 6,500+ students in hands-on space missions
- 100+ government schools engaged
- 10,000 saplings planted (Social Forest); goal of 1 crore (10 million) trees
- 2 world / national space records
- Global peace conference reached students in 14+ languages
- Mission presented at the United Nations (2026)
- Aligned with Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013 and UN SDGs 4, 5, 8, 13, 15 and 17

## Vision and mission

Vision: A developed India powered by young people who dream boldly, think scientifically and serve society — realising Dr. Kalam's Vision 2020.

1. Ignite scientific temper in schoolchildren, especially in government schools and underserved communities.
2. Make space real through genuine student missions.
3. Build leadership, employable skills and a lifelong reading habit.
4. Protect the environment and work toward a greener, self-reliant India.
5. Carry Dr. Kalam's message of peace and knowledge to students worldwide.

## Programmes

- Student CubeSat Challenge (2021, world record): about 1,500 students designed and launched 100 femto-satellites on a single high-altitude balloon from Rameswaram, with Space Zone India and the Martin Group. The Prime Minister sent a congratulatory message.
- APJ Abdul Kalam Students Satellite Launch Vehicle Mission (19 February 2023): more than 5,000 students, including 2,000 from 100+ government schools, built 150 PICO satellites flown on India's first student hybrid rocket from Chengalpattu district, Tamil Nadu. Partners: Space Zone India and the Martin Foundation.
- APJ Abdul Kalam Social Forest (ongoing): a one-crore tree movement; 10,000 saplings planted at Olakkuda village, Rameswaram, with the Tamil Nadu Coastal Security Group.
- Centres for Igniting Young Minds (ongoing): STEM and innovation hubs inside schools across several states.
- Skilling and Kalam Home Libraries (ongoing): career skilling for UG/PG students in IT, AI and Data Science, and Dr. Kalam Student's Home Libraries.
- Kalam International School (planned): a Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam International School at Rameswaram, plus sponsorship of underprivileged students and women-empowerment programmes.

## Conferences and recognition

- 2016, New Delhi: 1st Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Memorial Lecture with the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), "Technology Trends & Future Research Directions for India".
- 15 October 2020, online: Dalai Lama Peace Conference — "Working Together for a Peaceful World", on Dr. Kalam's 89th birth anniversary, live-streamed in 14+ languages.
- 2021, online: World Nature Conservation Day "Green" memorial lecture.
- 2023, national: TechXcelerate — Transforming Tomorrow, on AI, robotics and space technology (Dr. Kalam's 92nd birth anniversary).
- 2025, Kingdom of Bahrain: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam STEM / SPACE Conclave at the Al-Aayam Media Center; chief guest Dr. P. Veeramuthuvel, Chandrayaan-3 Project Director (ISRO).
- 2026, United Nations, New York: the foundation presented its mission of peace, youth empowerment and sustainable development.
- Also online: "AI for India — A Vision for a Developed Nation" with Dr. Raj Reddy and N.R. Narayana Murthy.

## Associations

ISRO, DRDO, Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Space Zone India, Martin Charitable Trust, Ministry of Science & Technology (Government of India), Tamil Nadu Coastal Security Group, Airports Authority of India, Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR), United Nations.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam International Foundation?

The Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam International Foundation is a registered public charitable trust based at the House of Kalam in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu. It carries forward the vision of Bharat Ratna Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, India's eleventh President, through STEM and space education, environmental work, skilling and peace programmes for young people, with a focus on government schools and underserved communities.

### When and where was the foundation established, and by whom?

The foundation was established on 11 October 2015 at the House of Kalam in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu, by the family and close colleagues of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.

### Who leads the Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam International Foundation?

The foundation is led by Chairperson Dr. A.P.J.M. Nazima Maraikayar, Co-Founders and Trustees APJMJ Sheik Dawood and APJMJ Sheik Saleem (grand-nephews of Dr. Kalam), and Secretary APJM Jainullabudeen. Its advisors include Y.S. Rajan, Prof. Sulthan Ahmed Ismail, Prof. N. Balakrishnan, Venkatarangan Thirumalai and Sasikumar Gendam.

### What programmes does the foundation run?

Its main programmes are student space missions (the 2021 Student CubeSat Challenge and the 2023 Satellite Launch Vehicle Mission), the APJ Abdul Kalam Social Forest tree-plantation movement, Centres for Igniting Young Minds (STEM hubs in schools), career skilling in IT, AI and Data Science, Dr. Kalam Student's Home Libraries, and a planned Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam International School at Rameswaram.

### What was the 2021 Student CubeSat Challenge world record?

In February 2021, around 1,500 students designed and launched 100 femto-satellites on a single high-altitude balloon from Rameswaram, organised by the foundation with Space Zone India and the Martin Group. It was recorded as a world first, and the Prime Minister sent a congratulatory message.

### What was the APJ Abdul Kalam Satellite Launch Vehicle Mission 2023?

On 19 February 2023, the foundation's student mission launched 150 PICO satellites, built by more than 5,000 students including 2,000 from over 100 government schools, on India's first student hybrid rocket from Chengalpattu district, Tamil Nadu. It was organised with Space Zone India and the Martin Foundation.

### What is the APJ Abdul Kalam Social Forest?

The APJ Abdul Kalam Social Forest is the foundation's tree-plantation movement with a goal of one crore (10 million) trees. 10,000 saplings have already been planted at Olakkuda village, Rameswaram, together with the Tamil Nadu Coastal Security Group.

### Can companies fund the foundation's work through CSR?

Yes. The foundation works as a CSR implementing partner for programmes eligible under Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013, including education and skills, environmental sustainability, rural development and reducing inequalities. It shares its 12A, 80G and CSR-1 credentials, audited accounts and a tailored proposal on request. Contact partnerships@apjabdulkalamfoundation.org.

### What global recognition has the foundation received?

The foundation presented its mission of peace, youth empowerment and sustainable development at the United Nations in New York in 2026, held its first overseas STEM / SPACE Conclave in the Kingdom of Bahrain in 2025, and hosted His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama at a 2020 peace conference live-streamed in more than 14 languages.

### How can students get involved or apply for an internship?

Students and early-career graduates can join the foundation's remote-friendly internship programme in content writing, social media, operations, human resources, event and programme support, or community outreach. Interns work on live projects, receive mentorship and earn a certificate of completion.

### How do I contact the Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam International Foundation?

Write to info@apjabdulkalamfoundation.org for general enquiries or partnerships@apjabdulkalamfoundation.org for CSR partnerships. The foundation's address is House of Kalam, Rameswaram – 623 526, Ramanathapuram District, Tamil Nadu, India.
